verdict.rationale: Proton Pass ships an official CLI, announced on its blog, that can create, update and delete items, including passwords and custom items. That gives an agent a first-party programmatic way to store and modify credentials. However, nothing shows the CLI can write TOTP secrets into entries; the 2FA support page only says the app generates TOTP codes for saved logins. Missing for 10: documented TOTP-secret seeding via the CLI, reference-level CLI documentation beyond a blog announcement, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven item writes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can create and update vault entries — seeding new TOTP secrets, storing credentials — through documented programmatic surfaces

citations.quote: View, create, update, and delete items including passwords, secure notes, credit cards, identities, WiFi entries, custom items, and stored SSH-key items
the CLI enables you to securely retrieve secrets and other items across scripts, deployments, and continuous integration/ continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
